headline: RBI releases 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Forex Reserves (Apr–Sep 2026)
summary_points: RBI has released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves, with reference to end-September 2026.
The practice of publishing these reports began in February 2004 to promote transparency and disclosure in reserves management.
During April-September 2026, India's forex reserves rose from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion.
The latest reserves position is available on the RBI website at the link given in the press release.
who_is_affected: Banks, treasury and forex teams, economists, and finance professionals who track India's external sector and reserves position.
action_required: No compliance action is needed; refer to the full report on the RBI website for detailed data on reserves management.

social.linkedin:
RBI has released the 47th Half-Yearly Report on Management of Foreign Exchange Reserves, with reference to end-September 2026.

Key takeaway: during April-September 2026, India's foreign exchange reserves increased from US$ 691.11 billion to US$ 737.78 billion.

RBI began compiling and publishing these half-yearly reports in February 2004 to promote greater transparency and enhance disclosure in the management of the country's forex reserves.

Why it matters: the reserves position is a key indicator of external sector strength and is closely watched by treasury teams, banks, finance professionals and policy observers.

There is no compliance action arising from this release, but the full report offers useful data for anyone tracking reserves management.

Press Release: 2026-2027/1564, dated 25 November 2026.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before relying on them.
